advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make check_repo_root_from_tracker.py report (not silently skip) files that fail ast.parse, so a scan failure is distinguishable from a clean result.
evidence:
scripts/check_repo_root_from_tracker.py:104-108: `    try:
        tree = ast.parse(source)
    except SyntaxError:
        return [], []`

The guard is wired into `make lint` as the enforcement boundary for AC#4; a parse failure produces the same empty result as a genuinely-clean file, so the check cannot distinguish 'scanned and clean' from 'could not scan'.
advisory.finding: scan_file() in the new AST guard returns ([], []) on SyntaxError, so a source file that fails to parse is silently treated as having no violations. A future dirname(tracker) site introduced in a file that also happens not to parse (or is broken by an unrelated edit) escapes the gate, and the guard's clean verdict is indistinguishable from 'the file was never actually scanned'.
scenarios: A src/*.py file with a syntax error (or one using syntax newer than the running interpreter) is skipped silently, and any dirname(tracker) composition inside it passes the gate.
advisory.suggested_fix: On SyntaxError, print a diagnostic to stderr and return a sentinel that forces a non-zero exit (or raise), rather than returning ([], []) which is identical to the clean case.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a unit test that feeds the guard a dirname(tracker) sample (flagged), a sanctioned sample (allowed), and a bare-marker sample (reported).
evidence: search_files for 'check_repo_root_from_tracker' under tests/ returned (no matches).
The patch adds the guard and wires it into `make lint` (Makefile) but adds no test exercising scan_file/find_violations/_marked.
advisory.finding: The new AST lint guard (scripts/check_repo_root_from_tracker.py) has no accompanying test. Its detection of the two flagged shapes, its honoring of the '# repo-root-ok: <reason>' sanction, and its rejection of a bare marker are all unverified, so a regression in the guard (e.g. the fail-open SyntaxError path or a broken _marked window) would go unnoticed.
scenarios: Someone refactors _store_shape, _marked, or _DIRNAME_CALLEES and inadvertently stops detecting the flagged shape; no test catches it.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a self-test for scripts/check_repo_root_from_tracker.py (mirroring test_tickets_boundary_guard.py) pinning: dirname(tracker) and dirname(*.tracker_dir()) flagged, prose/docstring not flagged, reasoned `# repo-root-ok:` sanctioned, bare `# repo-root-ok` reported as no-reason.
evidence: New file scripts/check_repo_root_from_tracker.py adds a 209-line AST guard with _store_shape/_marked/_Visitor discrimination logic

The sibling guard it explicitly mirrors IS tested: tests/unit/test_tickets_boundary_guard.py:22 `_SCRIPT = _REPO_ROOT / "scripts" / "check_tickets_boundary.py"` with parametrized composition-vs-prose discrimination tests

Named violating inputs the guard must classify and no test asserts: `os.path.dirname(tracker)` (violation), `os.path.dirname(reads.tracker_dir())` (violation via tracker_dir shape), a `# repo-root-ok: <reason>` line (sanctioned), a bare `# repo-root-ok` (reported no-reason at scripts/check_repo_root_from_tracker.py:97-100), and a docstring/comment mentioning `dirname(tracker)` (must NOT flag)
advisory.finding: The new AST lint guard scripts/check_repo_root_from_tracker.py (209 added lines) has no test, unlike its documented sibling check_tickets_boundary.py which carries tests/unit/test_tickets_boundary_guard.py pinning the same discrimination. Its novel logic — _store_shape (the `tracker` name vs `*.tracker_dir()` call), the `# repo-root-ok:` sanction requiring a mandatory reason, bare-marker reporting, and the statement-line marker scan — is entirely unexercised, so a regression (e.g. the AC#4 run_sweep allowlist silently ceasing to match, or prose being flagged) ships green.
scenarios: A future edit to _store_shape or _DIRNAME_CALLEES stops matching a real composing site, disabling AC#4 enforcement with no failing test
The sanction-marker scan (_marked) regresses so a bare marker is silently accepted, or a valid reasoned sanction is rejected
advisory.suggested_fix: Create tests/unit/test_repo_root_from_tracker_guard.py that imports check_repo_root_from_tracker and runs find_violations / scan_file over synthetic src trees covering each shape, the sanction marker, and the bare-marker case.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add relocated-store regression tests (or correct the docstring) for delete.py scratch cleanup and validate.py signature verification, the remaining sites the fix touches.
evidence: test_relocated_store_repo_root.py:6-7 docstring claims coverage of 'the CLI dispatcher's repo_root, scratch cleanup on delete, and the library clarity-check threshold'
The file contains only three test functions: transition gate, clarity threshold, and gate-off contrast — none exercise delete.py scratch cleanup or the _cli/_execute.py argv_tracker_root dispatcher
delete.py:390 `scratch.cleanup_for_ticket(repo_root, ticket_id)` is a changed line with no relocated-store test asserting scratch is resolved under the repo root
validate.py:124 `repo_root=config.repo_root_or_none()` changed with no test in the diff
advisory.finding: Two changed production sites — delete.py scratch cleanup (scratch.cleanup_for_ticket now uses repo_root instead of os.path.dirname(tracker)) and validate.py signature verification (repo_root=config.repo_root_or_none()) — have no relocated-store test, though the docstring of the new test file claims to pin 'scratch cleanup on delete' as one of the sites.
scenarios: A relocated store where delete.py's repo_root threading regresses back to dirname(tracker) would not be caught
The _cli/_execute.py dispatcher passing None (vs dirname) is asserted only indirectly

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update tests/unit/test_cli_registry_dispatch.py:150 (and its docstring) to expect the dispatcher's new third argument `None` instead of `"/repo"`.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_execute.py diff: `-        return fn(rest, tracker, os.path.dirname(tracker))` / `+        return fn(rest, tracker, None)`
tests/unit/test_cli_registry_dispatch.py:150 `assert seen == [(["abcd"], "/repo/.tickets-tracker", "/repo")]` — expects dirname `"/repo"`, but the dispatcher now emits `None`
tests/unit/test_cli_registry_dispatch.py:141 docstring still says argv_tracker_root handlers `get (rest, tracker, dirname)`
advisory.finding: The `argv_tracker_root` dispatcher now passes `None` as the root argument (`_execute.py`: `return fn(rest, tracker, None)`), but the existing test `test_argv_tracker_root_adapter_appends_tracker_and_root` still asserts the emitted third argument equals `"/repo"` (the old `os.path.dirname(tracker)` value). This test was not updated in the diff and will now fail — the emitted dispatch shape changed without updating its consuming assertion.
scenarios: Running the unit suite after this change: the dispatcher emits None, the assertion expects "/repo", the test fails.
advisory.suggested_fix: Change the assertion to `assert seen == [(["abcd"], "/repo/.tickets-tracker", None)]` and update the docstring from `(rest, tracker, dirname)` to `(rest, tracker, None)`.

blocking.finding: bugfix-size-attestation: this change touches 273 non-test line(s) — over the 150-line floor for a bug fix — but bug 2ec7-be89-9b01-496a has no acceptable plan-review attestation (verdict: unsigned; no plan-review attestation record). A fix like this is a design change wearing a bug label: write the fix plan into the ticket's description, run `rebar review-plan 2ec7-be89-9b01-496a` (it auto-escalates a bug with non-test file impact to the full review and SIGNS an attestation on a PASS; if the review passed but no attestation landed, `rebar sign-review 2ec7-be89-9b01-496a` re-persists it cheaply, and `rebar review-plan 2ec7-be89-9b01-496a --status` confirms it is current without an LLM call), then re-push.
